question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(t)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(t)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{3t-9}{{t}^{2}+t-12}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\frac{3t-9}{{t}^{2}+t-12} \\  & =\frac{3(t-3)}{(t-3)(t+4)} \\  & =\frac{3\cancel{(t-3)}}{\cancel{(t-3)}(t+4)} \\  & =\frac{3}{t+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the numerator equal to zero, we get $3=0,$ which is a false statement. Therefore, $f(t)=0$ has no solution, and so $f(t)$ has no roots.
